<reason>Both sides were sharp and narrowed the clash well. PRO's best work was reframing the motion as narrow (voluntary telematics survives) and catching CON conceding the fair terms — resale bans, secondary-use bans, location-scoring bans, rate review — so that only the surcharge-for-refusal clause remained contested. PRO's Pressure Q1 also landed a genuine hit, forcing CON to admit sorting rather than behavior change is the "bigger and faster" saving, which deflated CON's crash-victims weighing. But CON identified the true marginal content of the motion ("a rule about use is not the motion") and attacked it on its own terms with two durable arguments: (1) an accurate price for a self-selected residual pool is ordinary adverse selection, with a real ceiling (expected cost plus rate review), which answered PRO's voluntariness question directly; and (2) the counterfactual is not privacy but proxy pricing — ZIP, credit, occupation — which the motion leaves fully intact while removing the one factor a driver can rebut with. Decisively, CON turned PRO's own concession in [A4.1] (that the unmonitored rate may rise later on claims experience) into a contradiction: the refuser is priced anyway, and priced on the average of everyone else who refused — the group averaging PRO called "redlining in a behavioural costume." PRO's closing never answered that turn, and CON's closing reductio (if a price difference is a fine, all risk-based pricing is coercion) exposed that PRO's headline principle over-generalizes. PRO's document-versus-life distinction blunts but does not repair the internal inconsistency. CON therefore leaves the cleaner reason to vote, though PRO's concession-stack framing keeps the margin competitive.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's [B4.4]: taking PRO's concession that the unmonitored rate may legitimately rise "on that claims experience" and showing that this prices the refuser on the average of other refusers — reintroducing exactly the group averaging PRO condemned as redlining, and leaving PRO's fairness clause buying little beyond a lag. PRO's closing did not answer it.</best_rebuttal>
